This article analyzes data from Appendikstabel 5. Typer af kirurgiske indgreb foretaget på patienter med IBD (indikator 6), which catalogs the surgical interventions performed on patients treated within the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] [^src1]. The dataset captures procedures coded for [[ibd|IBD]] patients between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023 [^src1]. Because the evidence consists of a single dated section, no longitudinal trends can be established, and it is impossible to determine whether surgical preferences improved, declined, or remained flat over time [^src1]. Furthermore, the table records only raw counts and percentages without defining any clinical targets, thresholds, or quality standards, meaning no targets can be evaluated as met or missed [^src1].

Among the specific surgical procedures, laparoscopic colectomy and ileostomy (KJFH11) is the clear leader, performed 152 times and accounting for 16.6% of the reported operations [^src1]. The next most common procedures are laparoscopic ileocecal resection (KJFB21) with 106 operations (11.5%) and endoscopic dilation of the large intestine (KJFA58) with 100 operations (10.9%) [^src1]. At the other end of the spectrum, the trailers are three procedures tied for the lowest frequency, each performed only 5 times (0.5%): enteroenterostomy (KJFC00), conversion of ileoanal anastomosis to ileostomy (KJFF16), and laparoscopic excision of the rectum with ileoanal anastomosis after previous surgery (KJGB61) [^src1]. 

A significant outlier in the data is the "Øvrige" (Other) category, which aggregates 97 operations (10.6%) [^src1]. This catch-all classification represents a higher volume of surgeries than any individual procedure code except the top three, highlighting that a substantial minority of interventions fall outside the most frequently tracked specific surgical codes [^src1].
